questions.q: Why does this report's plan need five tables instead of four?
options: "Category" is not a column directly on Product -- it requires two hierarchy hops, through ProductSubcategory and then ProductCategory
Sales.SalesOrderDetail must always be joined to itself
AdventureWorks2012 requires every query to touch at least five tables
Production.Product has no ProductID column
questions.explain: Product only stores a ProductSubcategoryID; getting to a category name means joining up to ProductSubcategory and then up again to ProductCategory.

questions.q: What is the join key between Production.Product and Production.ProductSubcategory?
options: SalesOrderID
ProductID
ProductSubcategoryID
ProductCategoryID
questions.explain: Product stores a ProductSubcategoryID that points at the matching row in ProductSubcategory.

questions.q: Why does the plan start from Sales.SalesOrderDetail rather than Sales.SalesOrderHeader?
options: LineTotal, the amount being summed, lives on SalesOrderDetail, and starting there avoids double-counting an order's total once per line item
T-SQL requires FROM to start with whichever table has the most rows
Production.Product can only be joined directly to SalesOrderHeader
SalesOrderHeader does not contain an OrderDate column
questions.explain: An order with several line items produces several detail rows and only one header row; starting from detail avoids summing the order total multiple times.

questions.q: What happens to a product that has no ProductSubcategoryID assigned, given this query's INNER JOIN chain?
options: It causes the query to fail with an error
It drops out of the result entirely, because it can never reach a category name
It is automatically assigned to the Accessories category
It appears under a category called "Uncategorized"
questions.explain: Because every join in the chain is an INNER JOIN, a product that can't reach a ProductSubcategory row -- and therefore can't reach a category -- is excluded from the output, which is the correct behavior for a category performance report.

questions.q: What is this report's grouping (GROUP BY) column, per the plan?
options: Product name
OrderDate
Category name and territory name together
Category name alone -- a single-column grouping
questions.explain: Unlike a report split by both region and product line, this report's grain is one row per category, so the plan groups by category name alone.
